title: How I turn generated pixel-art blocks into usable sprites for Decknaut
author: Fantastic-Wrap-5176
selftext:
Decknaut is a browser deckbuilder I’m building. One art problem I ran into was that an image could look like pixel art at full size, then turn soft or uneven when I brought it down to sprite size. Here’s what the current import pipeline does.



For a 96×128 sprite canvas, I ask the OpenAI image model for a 1152×1536 image with roughly 12-pixel blocks. When redrawing an existing sprite, I first resize the reference to the target grid and enlarge it 12×, so the model has a grid to follow.



The importer estimates the spacing and offset of the block edges. It takes the most common colour from the inner half of each block and turns that into one actual sprite pixel. Sampling the middle avoids picking up the soft edges between blocks. If the grid is too weak to detect, the import fails so I can regenerate that asset.



The starship is wider than the model handles consistently on one grid, so it’s made from overlapping slices. The stitcher checks that the slices agree on block size. I also split detailed pieces into a reference pass and a grid redraw, since asking for fine detail and clean blocks in one pass tends to produce irregular pixels. Some card and event art still uses the older resize path, so the difference is visible in the beta.



You can see the ship and sprites in the free beta at https://decknaut.com/. The optional Supporter Pack is cosmetic. If you’ve tried a similar approach, how do you keep fine details like rivets readable across sprites at different sizes?
